\subsection*{Secret Sharing --- Defs: Results}

\begin{definition}[Monotone access structure]
\lean{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure}
\label{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure}
\leanok
An access structure on a set of parties specifies a collection of authorized finite
subsets, with the property that every finite superset of an authorized set is
authorized.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Cardinality threshold access structure]
\lean{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure.threshold}
\statementsource{Sha79}{pdf-a76120fbec44-p001-b005}
\statementsource{AL17}{pdf-27f2b3787521-p004-b002}
\label{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure.threshold}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure}
For a set of parties and a natural number $k$, the threshold access structure authorizes
exactly those finite subsets whose cardinality is at least $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Authorization in a threshold structure]
\lean{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure.threshold_auth}
\statementsource{AL17}{pdf-27f2b3787521-p004-b002}
\label{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure.threshold_auth}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure.threshold}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a type, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $A$ be a finite subset of $P$.
In the threshold access structure with threshold $k$, the set $A$ is authorized if and
only if its cardinality is at least $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Secret-sharing scheme]
\lean{TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme}
\statementsource{Sha79}{pdf-a76120fbec44-p002-b003}
\statementsource{BGW88}{
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b005,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b006
}
\label{TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme}
\leanok
A secret-sharing scheme for parties, secrets, shares, and randomness consists of a
sharing map that assigns a share to each party given a secret and random input, and a
reconstruction map that assigns a secret to each finite set of parties and each
party-indexed share assignment.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Correct reconstruction]
\lean{TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme.Correct}
\statementsource{Sha79}{
  pdf-a76120fbec44-p002-b002,
  pdf-a76120fbec44-p002-b003
}
\statementsource{BGW88}{
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b006,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p005-b006
}
\label{TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme.Correct}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure}
A secret-sharing scheme is correct for an access structure if, for every authorized
finite set of parties, every secret, and every random input, reconstructing from the
shares produced by the sharing map returns the original secret.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local reconstruction]
\lean{TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme.LocalReconstruct}
\label{TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme.LocalReconstruct}
\leanok
A secret-sharing scheme has local reconstruction if, for every finite set of parties and
any two assignments of shares that agree at every party in that set, reconstruction from
the set gives the same result for both assignments.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Perfect privacy]
\lean{TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme.PerfectPrivacy}
\statementsource{Sha79}{
  pdf-a76120fbec44-p001-b005,
  pdf-a76120fbec44-p002-b004
}
\statementsource{BGW88}{
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b005,
  pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b006
}
\label{TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme.PerfectPrivacy}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure}
A secret-sharing scheme has perfect privacy with respect to a monotone access structure
if, for every unauthorized finite set of parties and every two secrets, there is a
bijection of the randomness space such that each choice of randomness and its image
produce identical shares for every party in that set.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Equal view counts under perfect privacy]
\lean{TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme.PerfectPrivacy.card_view_eq}
\label{TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme.PerfectPrivacy.card_view_eq}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.SecretSharing.AccessStructure, TCSlib.SecretSharing.Scheme.PerfectPrivacy}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a type, let $\Gamma$ be an access structure on finite subsets of $P$, and let
$S$ be a secret-sharing scheme with secret type $\mathrm{Secret}$, share type
$\mathrm{Share}$, and randomness type $\mathrm{Rand}$. Suppose $S$ has perfect privacy
for $\Gamma$. For any unauthorized finite subset $B\subseteq P$, any two secrets
$\mathrm{sec},\mathrm{sec}'$, and any assignment $w:P\to\mathrm{Share}$, the sets of
random choices producing view $w$ on $B$ under the two secrets have equal cardinalities.
\end{theorem}
